thread:
miriam: heads up — customer on Dedicated (vpc-prod-us-west) reporting 401s when hitting our inference gateway through their LB + istio setup. they say it works when they call the worker directly but fails via the ingress path. escalating, they’re blocked in prod :frowning:
kevin: ok can you paste the failing request + curl output they sent? any prod id or request id we can trace?
miriam: here's the curl they sent (redacted key):

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_KEY" "https://inference.customers.example.com/v1/generate" -d '{"input":"hi"}'

Response: 401 Unauthorized, body: {"error":"missing authorization header"}

They also tried port-forwarding to the pod and the same curl works (200). So looks like header gets dropped somewhere in LB/ingress/Istio.
sasha: common culprits: ALB/nginx config, istio VirtualService or EnvoyFilter removing headers, or an ingress TLS redirect wiping headers. Also check if there’s an auth filter (JWT) rejecting it upstream and returning 401 instead of forwarding.
kevin: quick checks: 1) curl -v to ingress and check request/response headers on envoy ingress logs 2) compare to pod-level logs 3) check VirtualService/EnvoyFilter for header remove rules
miriam: customer provided envoy ingress logs attached (snippet):

[2026-04-01T18:12:45Z] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 401 - - "-" 0 0 0 "-" "curl/7.68.0" "-"

But no Authorization shows in the recorded request headers in that log. they also captured a tcpdump at the customer LB showing Authorization present when reaching LB.
kevin: run these commands in cluster to search for header-removal rules: 

kubectl get virtualservice --all-namespaces -o yaml | grep -i "remove:\|authorization" -n || true
kubectl get envoyfilter --all-namespaces -o yaml | grep -i authorization -n || true
also check any nginx config on the LB nodes: grep -R "proxy_set_header Authorization" /etc/nginx || true
sasha: i recall an operator accidentally added a VirtualService header remove for "authorization" to strip creds before an oauth sidecar. check history: kubectl get virtualservice redwood-ingress -n infra -o yaml
alex: i just ran a quick scan in prod infra namespace: found a VirtualService with request.headers.remove: [authorization] that was added 2 days ago as part of a canary for an internal auth-proxy. that would explain it.
miriam: oh wow — is that safe to remove? customer is on Dedicated VPC — changes may affect internal flows.
kevin: we need to assess impact. who owns that VirtualService change? annotated in git? alex, can you link the change/PR?
alex: PR: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/ingress-config/pull/298 — title "strip auth header for auth-proxy canary". owner: @sasha. It was intended to prevent double-auth for an internal path, but the match was too broad and applied to wildcard host.
sasha: yes i merged that by mistake with a broad host match — my bad. Mitigation options: 1) narrow the VS match to specific host/path for the internal proxy, 2) remove the remove: [authorization] line, or 3) add a header add on route to forward Authorization to upstream as x-authorization and have the internal auth-proxy expect that.
kevin: recommended quick unblock: revert the PR or patch the VirtualService to stop removing authorization for customer host(s). we should do a controlled rollout and test with curl against ingress. also alert the oncall for config rollback.
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0421-13 — customer auth header dropped on Dedicated ingress. assign: eng-platform oncall.
miriam: customer confirmed they can test if we patch; they can wait ~30m. i'll coordinate.
kevin: patch command (kubectl apply -f -):

cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: redwood-ingress
  namespace: infra
spec:
  hosts:
  - "inference.customers.example.com"
  http:
  - match:
    - uri:
        prefix: "/v1/"
    route:
    - destination:
        host: inference-upstream
    headers:
      request:
        remove: [] # ensure authorization not removed for this host
EOF

kevin: after apply, test:
1) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_KEY" https://inference.customers.example.com/v1/generate
2) kubectl logs -l app=istio-ingressgateway -n istio-system | tail -n 200 to verify request shows header

sasha: rolling patch now, will watch metrics and envoy logs. tagging @oncall
kevin: i recommend also adding an automated grep across VS/EnvoyFilter to detect any future accidental remove: [authorization] and a small unit test in infra CI that rejects wildcard host matches for header-removal rules.
miriam: customer: patch applied, test now... they say it works — 200 returned. they ran an end-to-end job and back to green. :tada:
alex: i pushed a follow-up PR to narrow the original canary to host internal-auth.example.com and added a comment in the VS explaining intent.
sasha: sorry about that, will add a checklist for VS changes and require one extra reviewer for header transforms. also adding an alert: config drift rule to search for header removals.
kevin: good. runbook items: 1) diagnostic checklist (curl direct pod vs ingress, ingress logs, kubectl search for remove: authorization, check EnvoyFilter), 2) quick patch snippet, 3) CI lint rule, 4) postmortem with timeline and owner
miriam: i'll send the customer a summary and postmortem once we finalize. closing the escalation when we have runbook + PRs merged. thanks everyone.
alex: noted for postmortem, will add timeline to INC-2026-0421-13.

[end of thread]
